catalogue_requests.summary: Send OUT1234:0 to all four outputs through the native send path; the safe state.

notes:
Passed on the fake backend with python3 -m mhs.driver check; evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. No hardware was attached, the hardware backend of native.py was never imported or run, and every fake value is test data marked '# placeholder'. The package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null); a human must review it before hardware use. The upstream has no simulator and no tests, so fake.py is an in-memory stand-in for the KC3405P methods the driver calls. The driver controls one of the four output channels: the channel is the backend option 'channel' (default 1) and channels 2 to 4 are NOT COVERED by this binding; get_settings/status still report all four. The catalogue has no dedicated power-supply kind, so device_kind is instrument.smu, the closest kind whose resource_kinds let cap.measure.voltage.v1 and cap.measure.current.v1 bind. No text of the clone states an output voltage, output current, overvoltage-protection or overcurrent-protection range; the class constants are starting values, not bounds, so all four numeric writes are Limit.operator_required and are refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET until the operator writes site-limits.json. site-limits.example.json supplies example-only operator bounds (0-30 V and 0-5 A) and is what G8 serves; those numbers are not device facts. The upstream set_overcurrent_protection and set_overvoltage_protection verify the current/voltage setpoint instead of the protection setting they write (korad.py:193-196 and 208-211); the driver calls those public setters and then reads the protection setting back, so a native exception is never hidden, but a spurious upstream ValueError would surface as a failed write. The e-stop and the safe-state action send OUT1234:0 through the native _send_command path without waiting for a STATUS? reply; the ordinary disable_output path waits on a blocking receive. The physical stop stays authoritative and OpenMHS is not a safety certification. There is no array to leave uncovered. No catalogue class fits the safe-state output stop, so x-cap.steinkohl.output_off.v1 is requested in catalogue_requests.
